query: For initially solid FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles exposed to the premelting and melting regime, the limited understanding of their thermal response prevents clear definition of their usable temperature range and behavior during high-temperature synthesis. What single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs the onset and progression of their phase transition and why? Specify a controlled comparison, predicted observations relative to the starting baseline, relevant boundary conditions, supporting evidence from prior nanoparticle studies, and a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The onset and progression of premelting and melting in FeNiCrCoCu high‐entropy‐alloy nanoparticles are governed by surface segregation of the lowest‐melting‐point element (Cu), which locally reduces the surface melting temperature and nucleates a liquid‐like layer that propagates inward.
generation.material_initial_state: Solid, single‐phase, equiatomic FeNiCrCoCu HEA nanoparticles (∼5 nm diameter) with uniform elemental distribution and fully crystalline interior.
generation.intervention: Rapid thermal ramp (∼10 K/s) in UHV from room temperature to above the bulk HEA melting point (∼1600 K).
generation.conditions: Particle sizes 3–10 nm; UHV (<10^–7 Torr); heating rate ≤100 K/s; no surface‐active adsorbates; in situ TEM imaging and EDS mapping.
generation.structural_mediator: Surface‐segregated Cu enrichment forming a subnanometer liquid‐like shell prior to core melting.
generation.mechanism: Cu atoms diffuse and accumulate at the surface under heating, lowering local melting enthalpy and initiating a liquid‐like layer that deepens and advances into the particle as temperature increases.
generation.predicted_outcome: 1) Onset of premelting at temperatures 50–150 K below the bulk HEA melting point. 2) In situ EDS will show a 10–30 at.% increase in surface Cu concentration at the premelting temperature. 3) Direct TEM imaging will reveal a few‐Å‐thick disordered (liquid‐like) surface layer prior to core collapse.
generation.baseline: Uniform, fully crystalline nanoparticles showing no detectable disorder or phase change below the bulk melting point.
generation.boundary: Applies to equiatomic FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles 3–10 nm in diameter under UHV heating rates ≤100 K/s; may not hold for particles >20 nm or in reactive atmospheres.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate – the exact Cu surface enrichment threshold and the thickness of the premelt layer may vary with particle size and ramp rate.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize two sets of ∼5 nm FeNiCrCoCu HEA nanoparticles: one as‐prepared (uniform) and one pre‐treated to inhibit Cu surface segregation (e.g., via a conformal thin oxide or ligand shell). Perform identical in situ TEM heating experiments with EDS mapping during a 10 K/s thermal ramp to 1600 K.
measurements: Melting onset temperature (from bright‐field TEM contrast changes)
Surface and bulk elemental composition profiles (in situ EDS)
Thickness and morphology of any disordered surface layer (high‐resolution TEM)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If premelting occurs at the same temperature in both sets without any measurable Cu surface enrichment and without formation of a distinct surface liquid layer, the hypothesis is falsified.
